newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks end sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks end sharply higher.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks rallied Monday as the market overcame a sell-off in Boeing Co. to snap its three-session losing streak.

The Dow Jones industrial average rose 44.15 points to close at 6,783.02. In the broader market, advancing issues outnumbered declines 1,350 to 1,083 on moderate volume of about 402 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

Boeing, one of 30 stocks in the Dow, slid 6-5/8 to 95-3/8 after reporting earnings that disappointed investors and warned that production of newer aircraft was likely to keep profit margins under pressure for the near-term.
But that apparently did not concern most investors.

"It appears no one chose to draw the inference Boeing's problems will translate into the same kinds of problems for other companies," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co.
"That suggests there's still a high degree of confidence in this market," he said.
Interest rate-sensitive stocks, which would suffer the most should inflation pick up, put in a strong performance.
The gains, which were concentrated in bank shares, surprised some on Wall Street, coming as they did just ahead of an extremely heavy calendar of economic data.
"To some degree, people are placing their bets," said Peter Green, vice president of technical research at Gruntal & Co., "and those bets are interest rate-sensitive."
Among banks, Wells Fargo & Co. gained 8-5/8 to 259-1/4 and Citicorp rose 3-7/8 to 107-1/4.
Meanwhile, long-term interest rates edged lower, with the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond up 11/32, lowering its yield to 7.11 percent from Friday's close of 7.14 percent.
Beyond the upturn in bank stocks, the broad market's performance was cautious and mixed ahead of key economic data.
Due early Tuesday is the first quarter Employment Cost Index -- a closely watched barometer of wage inflation.
With employment, Gross Domestic Product and manufacturing numbers all due later in the week, analysts said the mood was likely to become even more cautious for the next few days.
"We still have a vary full plate in front of us," said Dick Stein, vice president at U.S. Clearing Corp. "This is a case where the other team has the ball and the rest of us play defence."
In individual issues, machine tool maker Giddings & Lewis Inc. jumped 6-47/64 to 20-23/64 after Harnischfeger Industries Inc. launched a $19-a-share tender offer for the company.
The jump in Giddings' stock suggested investors believed a higher bid would be forthcoming, but analysts expressed doubt. Harnischfeger fell 3-1/8 to 42-1/4.
Nike Inc. fell 2-3/4 to 53-3/8 after Hambrecht & Quist downgraded the stock, citing a weak U.S. market for the athletic footwear maker.

McDermott International Inc. and its affiliate J. Ray McDermott both failed to open for trading. McDermott said both companies would report larger-than-expected fourth quarter losses, and that it was probing allegations of wrongdoing by former employees, unrelated to the expected losses.
The Nasdaq composite index rose 7.74 points to 1,217.03.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 7.59 points to 772.96. The American Stock Exchange index was off 1.63 to 541.20.
The NYSE composite index of all listed common stocks rose 3.31 to 403.69. The average share was up 33 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,274.231, up 57.724 or 0.80 percent.
